title: X canonical URL caused full LLM regeneration
reproduction: A source begins as /i/status/<id> and acquisition resolves it to /<author>/status/<id>.
impact: The same valid director manifest was regenerated, adding 22 LLM calls and avoidable cost.

title: Missing browser text aborted an otherwise valid render
reproduction: A source page changes DOM text after the director selected an exact evidence target.
impact: Capture failed instead of preserving the source page with an honest non-highlighted fallback.

title: GitHub placeholder description became a fake browser target
reproduction: The GitHub API returns the literal placeholder 'No repository description'.
impact: The recorder searched for text that was never visible on the repository page.

title: Launchd lock contention was recorded as a pipeline crash
reproduction: A scheduled launch overlaps a still-running manual or launchd pipeline.
impact: A healthy no-op collision polluted the bug audit as a crash.

title: Sensitive research review could be confused with publication approval
reproduction: A security-research video reaches the dashboard with only the editorial safety gate blocked.
impact: One click could ambiguously mean both safety review and publication authorization.

title: Model video title named the publisher but omitted the model
reproduction: A repair shortens a model hook by dropping GLM-5.3-Flash while retaining OrcaRouter.
impact: Viewers cannot identify which model the metrics describe.

title: Specialist metric was not explained for vibe coders
reproduction: The hook says refusal rate or rejection rate with a percentage but never defines the metric.
impact: A technically curious non-research audience sees numbers without understanding what they measure.

title: Long exact titles risked losing entities instead of adapting layout
reproduction: A title needs the exact model name plus a quantified hook and exceeds the default two-line rail.
impact: Copy repair could remove the subject to fit instead of preserving meaning.

title: YouTube output could contain silent or truncated audio
reproduction: A rendered collection item fails AAC, audio duration, or audible-audio validation.
impact: A video could look complete while losing the original speech after the opening minutes.

title: Tiny browser highlight aborted deterministic rendering
reproduction: A valid source target such as License: produces a yellow outline narrower than the readable-line gate.
impact: A valid content manifest failed rendering even though the page position itself was useful evidence.

title: Selected glossary definition was stored but invisible on X card
reproduction: The root X shot carries a glossary definition in audience_copy while the card renders only full_translation.
impact: The manifest passed readability checks but the viewer never saw the promised explanation.

title: YouTube interview highlight downloaded the complete source before selection
reproduction: Generate a 60–180 second known-tech interview highlight from a 15–120 minute YouTube source.
impact: The factory downloaded the entire source before transcript selection, wasting bandwidth, time, storage, and retry cost.

title: X acquisition hid OpenCLI exit diagnostics
reproduction: The same OpenCLI X command succeeds directly but exits 69 when the Video Factory subprocess lacks browser automation access.
impact: The job reported only CalledProcessError, so operators could not distinguish a browser permission boundary from a bad URL or missing post.

title: Editorial agent stopped after a cheap model exhausted semantic repairs
reproduction: The primary low-cost writer produces three near-duplicate retention hooks and the independent copy critic rejects every bounded repair.
impact: A valid source required Codex intervention even though a stronger qualified model was available through a configured fallback provider; an explicit primary-provider choice incorrectly disabled that route.

title: LLM retry multiplication allowed one logical call to block for six minutes
reproduction: A provider returns empty or invalid content while each of three transport attempts waits for the former 120-second timeout.
impact: A 12-call primary plus 14-call fallback path could take many minutes without local CPU work or visible progress.

title: Temporal wording still implied an explicitly unproven causal link
reproduction: Evidence says an account was suspended after a configuration change and the author explicitly says they do not know whether the setup triggered it.
impact: Short-video copy such as '照做后被封' was likely to be read as causation even after replacing the stronger word '导致'.

title: Employee reply was promoted to an official company response
reproduction: A company employee replies from a personal X account inside a public discussion thread.
impact: Viewer-facing copy called the personal comment the company's first official response, overstating source identity and authority.

title: WeChat playback chrome covered the fixed title and conclusion rails
reproduction: View a 1080x1920 information-frame video full-screen in WeChat Channels on a phone with status chrome and the post-title/action overlay visible.
impact: The first title line overflowed beneath the top status area and the fixed conclusion collided with the WeChat post title, making essential copy unreadable.

title: WeChat publisher silently left the original-content declaration unchecked
reproduction: Submit a Tencent/WeChat Channels video through the pinned social-auto-upload runtime and inspect the original-content checkbox before the final publish click.
impact: The publisher reported success without applying the creator's required original-content declaration.

title: Expired WeChat cookie was misclassified as an uncertain submission
reproduction: Let Tencent upload-video reject an expired cookie before constructing the uploader after a stale preflight check reported valid.
impact: A definitely safe pre-submit failure became non-retryable, forcing manual batch repair and delaying publication.

title: One WeChat publish attempt opened the creator page four times
reproduction: Run an approved Tencent publish batch and count browser launches from batch preflight, CLI setup, uploader validation, and the real upload page.
impact: Redundant login probes slowed every publish, confused the operator, and repeatedly rotated the WeChat session cookie.

title: Normal video mastering ran a redundant MoneyPrinterTurbo render before FFmpeg
reproduction: Render an editorial or GitHub video and inspect the mastering path after the native visual track is complete.
impact: Every job paid for an unnecessary external Python render and inherited its task-directory, placeholder-timing, and subprocess failure modes even though FFmpeg rebuilt the final output from the original native visual.

title: Capture stopped when optional web-scroll-video patch markers changed
reproduction: Format or upgrade the pinned web-scroll-video runner so one exact source marker used by the padded-runner patch no longer matches.
impact: A cosmetic integration patch became a single point of failure and required Codex to repair the dependency adapter before any video could be produced.

title: Default Chinese font resolved to one developer's MoneyPrinterTurbo checkout
reproduction: Run composition outside /Users/clairehou/pyProjects without setting VIDEO_FACTORY_FONT.
impact: Rendering failed on otherwise valid macOS, Linux, Windows, CI, or container installations even when a Chinese-capable system font was available.

title: Equal shot timing ignored visible text density
reproduction: Generate a BGM-only story whose evidence shots all receive the same duration even though one screen contains several times more visible Chinese and technical text than another.
impact: Dense evidence disappeared before viewers could finish reading it, while sparse shots consumed the same amount of the fixed runtime. The persistent upper hook and lower conclusion are intentional and remain pinned.

title: Experimental Radar styling silently replaced the stable compositor
reproduction: Load an archived manifest after adding expanded layouts, glass glosses, crop zoom, badges, and camera motion directly to the default render path.
impact: Every existing video changed at once, making regressions indistinguishable from intentional redesign and removing the known-good rollback path.

title: Radar effects had no bounded render fallback
reproduction: A platform FFmpeg build rejects the focus-crop or animated transition filter graph.
impact: A cosmetic enhancement could abort the entire agent instead of returning a readable stable video and recording the degraded path.

title: Retention prompt forced conflict when a direct fact was the better opening
reproduction: Generate a short for a strong technical announcement whose evidence contains no honest incumbent conflict or surprising comparison.
impact: The writer could manufacture drama, competitor framing, or ROI instead of quickly reporting what happened.

title: Radar density routing crashed on the first real capture
reproduction: Frame an archived OpenRouter capture with radar_v2 so the compositor classifies a highlighted price-table shot.
impact: The renderer raised NameError before FFmpeg because density matching depended on an unimported regular-expression module.

title: Radar identifier badge covered the first evidence lines
reproduction: Inspect the first OpenRouter Radar frame with a category pill and long model identifier at the top of the evidence pane.
impact: The badge overlapped the page headline and price proof, reducing readability while trying to add navigation metadata.

title: Hugging Face thumbnail URL became a fake model identifier
reproduction: Render a model story whose archived image URL under /social-thumbnails/models appears before the actual Hugging Face repository URL.
impact: The on-screen direct badge displayed HF: social-thumbnails/models instead of the real owner/model path.

title: Empty Radar metadata rail reduced evidence height
reproduction: Render a tweet story such as Jeff Dean or Sam Altman with no package, repository, model identifier, or factual category label.
impact: The compositor still reserved 88 pixels and drew a link-only badge, adding noise while shrinking the real evidence pane.

title: External visual critic retried failing media payloads without a bounded fallback ladder
reproduction: Send four videos to an AI Studio app, retry the same internal error, split to two videos, then encounter a paid-key requirement in the multimodal playground.
impact: A production agent could loop on a broken session, repeatedly upload the same assets, or implicitly cross a billing boundary instead of degrading safely and asking for authorization.

title: Developer artifact extraction discarded type and provenance
reproduction: Extract a package, model, container, or repository identifier for the Radar metadata rail and receive only a presentation string.
impact: Adding new ecosystems required more display-oriented regex patches, while downstream validation could not distinguish artifact kind or trace the source used for the badge.

title: Radar generation silently reused a classic-profile content cache
reproduction: Generate a URL with the classic profile, then request the same URL with --render-profile radar_v2 without --refresh.
impact: The factory reported a successful Radar request while returning the old classic manifest and copy contract, so visual A/B results were not actually generated by Radar V2.

title: Mechanical Radar contract errors consumed repeated LLM repair calls
reproduction: Return an otherwise grounded Radar brief with an unsupported label, over-budget visible copy, an invalid narrative beat, or a selected hook outside the candidate list.
impact: The agent repeatedly called writer and fallback models for deterministic formatting defects, increasing latency and cost while still failing to produce a manifest.

title: Radar validators disagreed on complete root-tweet translation length
reproduction: Generate a Radar X story whose complete first-post translation is valid under the 40–120 character root-card rule but exceeds the 40-character evidence-chip limit.
impact: Both primary and fallback writers were rejected for a translation that another contract explicitly required, making successful X generation impossible for substantive posts.

title: Web opening inherited the complete-tweet translation budget
reproduction: Generate an OpenRouter Radar story whose first browser shot contains a translation longer than 40 equivalents.
impact: The canonicalizer retained up to 120 equivalents as if the browser shot were a complete root tweet, while validation rejected it and exhausted both primary and fallback writers.

title: Subject-free Radar hooks incorrectly received the extended headline budget
reproduction: Generate a Radar hook longer than 20 equivalents that does not preserve any exact subject name.
impact: Canonicalization kept the hook under the 28-equivalent exception while validation correctly allowed that exception only for an exact model, project, or actor name, triggering an unnecessary fallback model.

title: Trailing punctuation in a model numeric field aborted the whole repair
reproduction: Receive a duration-like JSON string such as '0.605.' from a model repair response.
impact: A harmless sentence-ending period caused float conversion to fail after several successful calls, discarding the entire grounded draft and starting an expensive fallback model.

title: OpenRouter discount monitor was routed as a 50-second benchmark deep dive
reproduction: Route https://openrouter.ai/models?discount=true after the page text mentions benchmarks and evaluations.
impact: A price/news Radar request became a 25–50 second deep dive with the wrong single-header layout instead of a ten-second pinned-rail flash.

title: Copy critic re-reviewed the entire script when only a few fields were missing
reproduction: Have the critic omit several translation fields from an otherwise complete review, then repeat the same full review request.
impact: The second call was slower, could omit the same fields again, and forced a grounded Radar draft into the expensive fallback writer instead of completing the missing checks.

title: Radar width canonicalization severed a conclusion mid-claim
reproduction: Return a fixed conclusion longer than 40 equivalents whose width boundary falls inside a final named item such as Boris Cherny.
impact: The persistent takeaway rail displayed an incomplete name and could claim that there were three facts while showing only two, reducing both readability and factual integrity.

title: Audience glossary injection could overflow a canonical Radar shot
reproduction: Canonicalize a 40-equivalent Radar fact, then inject the required plain-language definition of refusal rate.
impact: A deterministic readability enhancement made the same shot fail the deterministic screen budget and triggered repeated semantic repair calls.

title: Radar hook required an entire delivery-suffixed model artifact name
reproduction: Use a model subject such as GLM-5.3-Flash-Uncensored-FP8 while the mobile hook names the exact base model GLM-5.3-Flash.
impact: The validator rejected a factual, readable title because the full artifact suffix could not fit the mobile headline budget.

title: A context event could be both required and discarded
reproduction: Receive a context graph that places the same event ID in required_context_ids and discarded_context_ids.
impact: Canonicalization selected the required event while validation simultaneously treated it as leaked discarded research, making the brief impossible to satisfy.

title: Readable Flash timing was rejected for exceeding an aspirational ten-second target
reproduction: Generate a complete three-shot Flash whose balanced evidence holds need 11.6 seconds against a 10-second target.
impact: The factory discarded a valid concise story and invoked a rate-limited fallback model instead of honoring the product rule to hold denser screens slightly longer.

title: Copy critic shorthand paths looked like omitted translation reviews
reproduction: Have the semantic critic return evidence_shots[0].translation instead of the requested editorial_brief.evidence_shots[0].translation path.
impact: All translation checks were present but discarded as unknown aliases, so the agent repeated the review and then abandoned both primary and fallback drafts.

title: Generation cache validated migrations but copied stale JSON into the job
reproduction: Load a cached manifest that is normalized by the current serializer, pass validation, and then create a new job from that cache hit.
impact: The in-memory fixed conclusion passed validation while the new job still received the old truncated conclusion from disk.

title: Direct-fact openings were forced to manufacture a conflict
reproduction: Return a grounded Radar brief with opening_mode=direct_fact and an intentionally empty attention_strategy.conflict.
impact: The validator contradicted the adaptive opening contract and sent a complete factual update into semantic repair solely to invent tension.

title: Multi-model price monitor was forced into a single-model headline
reproduction: Generate the OpenRouter discount index while its brief contains several model subjects and the hook correctly describes the cross-provider price page.
impact: The generic model validator selected one batch model as the mandatory subject and rejected the more accurate price-monitor story angle.

title: Copy critic shot-ID field paths were discarded as unknown
reproduction: Have the critic return shot-1.translation rather than editorial_brief.evidence_shots[0].translation.
impact: Valid per-shot semantic reviews were treated as omissions, causing a redundant supplemental review and eventual fallback failure.

title: Fallback writer and critic shared the same OpenRouter failure domain
reproduction: Escalate from a DeepSeek writer to an OpenRouter Gemini writer while the reviewer selector also chooses another OpenRouter model.
impact: An OpenRouter timeout or malformed review could take down both fallback generation and independent review, discarding an otherwise recoverable draft.

title: Radar screen budget rendered optional copy as sentence fragments
reproduction: Place a near-40-equivalent fact above an optional audience line such as 'OpenRouter 模型库可直接筛选折扣线路'.
impact: The canonicalizer filled the few remaining equivalents with fragments such as 'OpenRouter 模' or '单价降至每秒', making the finished frame look broken.

title: UI rerender silently re-authored an approved story
reproduction: Rerender an approved manifest with a new compositor while rerender still calls canonicalize_editorial_brief.
impact: A visual-only change could replace the hook, conclusion, evidence copy, or shot order and make a better-looking video tell a different story.

title: High-attention hook optimization abandoned the selected story axis
reproduction: Start with a people-change angle about Jeff Dean and three Google collaborators, then let the critic demand a hook different from the descriptive headline.
impact: The hook, conclusion, and final payoff pivoted from the Google team move to Discovery Loop's secondary parallel-experiment capability.

title: Direct OpenRouter discount-page generation bypassed the high-discount selection gate
reproduction: Generate the OpenRouter discount index directly while the most prominent current promotion is only 15% off.
impact: A routine promotion became a finished news video even though the product only wants exceptional price anomalies such as the verified 85.8% same-model saving.

title: Causal-safety copy replaced the bridge in a multi-party reply chain
reproduction: Tell the Sam Altman/Tibo account-suspension thread in three shots and omit Tibo's intervening reply while using a screenshot-proof disclaimer as the conclusion.
impact: Viewers saw Sam praise Tibo, an account suspension, and an Anthropic hiring reply without the response that explains why those events belong in one story.

title: Radar headline width clipping produced an unfinished hook
reproduction: Clip a hook such as '用户照 Tibo 的配置把 Claude Code 接到 GPT-5.6 Sol 后账号被停用' at the mobile width boundary.
impact: The permanent top rail ended at '接到', so the most important sentence looked broken even though the writer had supplied a complete shorter headline.

title: Both writer tiers exhausted repairs while omitting one reply-chain actor
reproduction: Ask the primary and fallback writers to preserve alex, Tibo, Boris, and Sam in one short event chain; each repair continues to omit Tibo or Boris.
impact: The agent correctly refused an unclear story but still required Codex intervention instead of recovering from its own structured subjects and evidence links.

title: Event-chain fallback dropped required context labels while preserving their evidence
reproduction: Rebuild a multi-party chain from subjects after context research marked the quoted setup and appeal posts as required.
impact: The facts remained visible, but exact causal setup validation rejected the fallback because context_event_ids were not migrated with overlapping evidence.

title: Copy critic demanded the same harness glossary in every visible field
reproduction: Use the specialist term harness in a hook, conclusion, and evidence translation after the first relevant shot can carry one adjacent definition.
impact: Repeated glossary demands overflowed mobile rails and exhausted both writer tiers even though one explanation was sufficient for comprehension.

title: Optional invented direct identifier exhausted an otherwise valid story
reproduction: Return a strong grounded brief plus a direct_identifier that cannot be found verbatim in archived evidence.
impact: An optional metadata badge consumed semantic repair rounds and blocked the entire video instead of safely disappearing.

title: Manifest loading rewrote story before a UI-only rerender
reproduction: Load an approved Radar manifest for rerender after disabling canonicalization only in the scene recompilation method.
impact: The loader still clipped an approved Sam event-chain fact to an unfinished phrase before the visual renderer received it.

title: Person-first hook assumed a technical figure was already famous
reproduction: Lead a Jeff Dean departure story with 'Jeff Dean announced' even though Google is the more recognizable audience anchor.
impact: The hook read like a neutral bulletin and gave mainland viewers no immediate reason to care.

title: Discount video treated low price as sufficient production guidance
reproduction: Describe a 90% OpenRouter discount without the model workload or route-specific uptime and response-time question.
impact: Developers learned the price but not whether the route fit their work or could safely serve production traffic.

title: Company conflict was diluted into a sequence of personal replies
reproduction: Tell the Sam/Tibo/Boris thread without naming OpenAI and Anthropic in the hook.
impact: The strongest reason to stop scrolling—the public tension between two AI vendors—disappeared.

title: Original-post Chinese translation was unreadably small on mobile
reproduction: Render a root X-card translation at 21–27px on a 1384px intermediate card and then scale it down into a 1080px WeChat frame.
impact: The most important Chinese explanation was technically present but not comfortably readable on a phone.

title: A fixed 40-character screen budget removed useful context instead of adding reading time
reproduction: Apply the same 40-equivalent limit to every two-to-four-second evidence shot regardless of typography and duration.
impact: The system produced sparse but shallow cards while other readable videos kept larger type and simply held denser screens longer.

title: Category pills displaced useful date context in time-sensitive flash videos
reproduction: Render a current X/news Flash with a large generic category capsule and a second link-hint capsule in the metadata rail.
impact: The interface looked templated while viewers could not see when the news happened.

title: A concrete earlier Google departure was rewritten as an abstract talent-war summary
reproduction: Use the Axios headline 'Google takes the hit in AI's talent war' as a visible pattern beat without opening the sourced event details.
impact: Viewers heard that Google was under pressure but never learned who left, where they went, or why the current four-person startup was part of a sequence.
